styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old town, fortifications and world-class museums.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: UNESCO walls, casemates and WWII memory.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Valley walks, parks and the Grund below the city.

stays.why: Inside the old town: walk to the Bock, casemates and Grand Ducal Palace. Quiet at night, few budget rooms.
Around the main station: most hotels, best value, free tram and buses to the centre in minutes.
Modern business district with big hotels and museums; good for parking and the EU quarter.
The old lower town in the valley: pretty, quiet and close to nightlife; steep walk or lift up to the centre.

food: Try Luxembourgish classics: judd mat gaardebounen (smoked pork with broad beans), gromperekichelcher potato fritters and bouneschlupp soup.
Look for a 'Kniddelen' or 'Mettwurst' lunch in the old town; portions are big, so share.
Place d'Armes and the Grund have the densest café and restaurant clusters; book dinner on weekends.
Cheap eats: bakery sandwiches, kebab and Asian lunch spots near the Gare, roughly EUR 8–15 a meal.
Wine and beer are local: try a Moselle wine or a Luxembourgish craft beer. Prices in the centre are high, so compare menus.
more_time: Day trip to Vianden: castle and river valley, roughly an hour by train and bus; check connections on the day.
Add a half-day to the Moselle wine villages (Remich, Grevenmacher) by bus or car.
History fans can swap a museum for the American Military Cemetery in Hamm or the Schueberfouer fair if it is on.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the old town, casemates and museums with a valley walk; add a night for a Vianden or Moselle day trip.

month_notes: Cold and grey: highs near 4°C, some rain or snow. Pack a warm coat and plan museum time.
Still cold, highs around 7°C, fewer rain days. Good for indoor sights and quiet streets.
Warming slowly to 10°C with rain. Bring layers and waterproof shoes for the valley paths.
Mild at 13°C, spring flowers in the parks. Showers are common, so carry a small umbrella.
Pleasant at 17°C, good walking weather. Rain is still likely on some days.
Warm and green at 22°C, long evenings. Best month for outdoor cafés and valley walks.
Warmest month, highs near 23°C. Book hotels early; summer weekends fill up.
Similar to July at 24°C, the peak for outdoor plans. Expect some rain days.
Cooling to 19°C, still good for walking. Fewer crowds than midsummer.
Autumn colours at 15°C with more rain. Bring a jacket and check the forecast.
Cold and wet at 9°C, the rainiest stretch. Indoor sights and warm cafés.
Dark and cold, highs near 6°C, most rain days. Christmas markets are the draw; dress warmly.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate and changeable: mild summers, cold winters and rain in every month. Pack layers and a rain jacket year-round.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Highs of 19–24°C and the most daylight. Ideal for the old town, valley walks and outdoor cafés.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: About 10–15 rain days a month, most in November to January. A light waterproof beats an umbrella in wind.

items.title: Cold winters
items.text: December to February highs of 4–7°C and lows near 0°C. Snow is possible but not guaranteed; check on the day.

items.title: Layers are key
items.text: Days can swing from cool mornings to warm afternoons. Bring a jacket even in summer evenings.

items.title: Long summer days
items.text: July and August give late sunsets, good for evening walks on the ramparts and in the Grund.

items.title: Winter charm
items.text: December is cold and wet but festive, with Christmas markets in the centre. Dress for damp cold.

transit.best: Walk the compact centre; use the free tram and buses for the airport, Gare and Kirchberg.

modes.text: No metro. The city is small and covered by tram and bus.
Buses 1–31 serve the city and most stop at Hamilius and Gare. Free to ride.
Tram T1 links the airport to the centre and Gare every 8 minutes. Free.
Taxis exist but are limited; Uber and Bolt operate. Handy for late nights and heavy bags.
Easy driving, but centre parking is paid and scarce on weekends. Best for day trips outside the city.
Great option: the centre is compact and bike-friendly, though the Grund sits in a steep valley.
No ferries; the country is landlocked.
